     3	This ledger maps labels of the manuscript on the second moment of the
     4	Stratonovich hyperbolic Anderson model with Gaussian noise fractional in time
     5	to the Lean declarations in this package. Labels and TeX line numbers refer to
     6	the manuscript revision a284420, and labels are written exactly as in its
     7	LaTeX source (for example `P:clock-copy-obstruction`). The ledger was written
     8	and reviewed at the earlier revisions cf979d6, 669ccc9, ba01d98, 3920258 and
     9	975feb3. Revision a284420 makes two mathematical edits that the ledger
    10	follows. (1) In `notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex` it adds Lemma
    11	`L:spatial-fourier-bound` (lines 101-164, display `E:spatial-fourier-bound`),
    12	the deterministic bound `A_sp(g) <= 2^(1+alpha) R_alpha b^(alpha/2)` that
    13	`SpatialFourierBound` already proved, and the proof of
    14	`P:spatial-smooth-ratio` (same label and statement) now derives `R_0 < inf`
    15	from it, independently of the finiteness of `S_1^pos`, which it keeps only
    16	for the score inequality. (2) In the main file, `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`
    17	replaces its smoothing and truncation sentence by the multiplier comparison
    18	`E:damped-multiplier-comparison` (a measurable multiplier `m` in `[0,1]`,
    19	nested measurable Laplace domains, positivity after time integration,
    20	scaling asserted only for the original covariance) and its proof by the
    21	corresponding argument. The other changes since 975feb3 are prose and front
    22	matter (title, abstract, preface, a theory-outlook chapter, the reader
    23	edition, Appendices F and G, the list of notation moved to the back).

   261	theorem uniform_series_tail_paper [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
   262	    (Y : ℝ → ℝ → ℕ → Lp ℝ 2 μ) (X : ℕ → Lp ℝ 2 μ) (r B : ℝ) (hr : 1 < r)
   263	    (hTW : ∀ ε δ : ℝ, 0 < ε → 0 < δ → TerminalWickInput μ (Y ε δ) r)
   264	    (hB : ∀ ε δ : ℝ, 0 < ε → 0 < δ →
   265	      ∫ ω, ((∑' n, r ^ n • Y ε δ n : Lp ℝ 2 μ) ω) ^ 2 ∂μ ≤ B)
   266	    (hX : ∀ n, Tendsto (fun p : ℝ × ℝ => Y p.1 p.2 n)
   267	      (𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ) ×ˢ 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ)) (𝓝 (X n))) :
   268	    (Summable fun n => ‖X n‖) ∧
   269	      Tendsto (fun p : ℝ × ℝ => ∑' n, Y p.1 p.2 n)

   273	      (∀ ε δ : ℝ, 0 < ε → 0 < δ → ∀ N : ℕ,
   274	        ‖∑' n, Y ε δ (n + (N + 1))‖ ≤ Real.sqrt B * (r ^ (N + 1))⁻¹ / (1 - r⁻¹)) ∧

   276	        Real.sqrt B * (r ^ (N + 1))⁻¹ / (1 - r⁻¹)) ∧
   277	      (∀ ε δ : ℝ, 0 < ε → 0 < δ → Summable fun n => ‖Y ε δ n‖) := by
   278	  have hr0 : 0 < r := lt_trans zero_lt_one hr
   279	  have hpos' : ∀ ε δ : ℝ, 0 < ε → 0 < δ → ∀ m n, 0 ≤ inner ℝ (Y ε δ m) (Y ε δ n) :=
   280	    fun ε δ hε hδ m n => by
   281	      rw [← integral_mul_eq_inner]; exact (hTW ε δ hε hδ).mixed_moment_nonneg m n
   282	  have hB' : ∀ ε δ : ℝ, 0 < ε → 0 < δ → ‖∑' n, r ^ n • Y ε δ n‖ ^ 2 ≤ B :=
   283	    fun ε δ hε hδ => by rw [← integral_sq_eq_norm_sq]; exact hB ε δ hε hδ
   284	  have hYb : ∀ ε δ : ℝ, 0 < ε → 0 < δ → ∀ n, ‖Y ε δ n‖ ≤ Real.sqrt B * (r ^ n)⁻¹ :=
   285	    fun ε δ hε hδ => term_bound (Y ε δ) r B hr0 (hTW ε δ hε hδ).abs_summable
   286	      (hpos' ε δ hε hδ) (hB' ε δ hε hδ)
   287	  have hgen := uniform_series_tail (𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ) ×ˢ 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ))
   288	    (fun p n => Y p.1 p.2 n) X r B hr
   289	    (eventually_pos_pair.mono fun p hp => (hTW p.1 p.2 hp.1 hp.2).abs_summable)
   290	    (eventually_pos_pair.mono fun p hp => hpos' p.1 p.2 hp.1 hp.2)
   291	    (eventually_pos_pair.mono fun p hp => hB' p.1 p.2 hp.1 hp.2) hX
   292	  obtain ⟨-, hXb, hXs, hXt, hlim⟩ := hgen
   293	  exact ⟨hXs, hlim, hYb, hXb,
   294	    fun ε δ hε hδ => (tail_bound (Y ε δ) _ r hr (hYb ε δ hε hδ)).2, hXt,

   297	/-- The last sentence of `L:uniform-series-tail` (TeX lines 3725-3726; proof
   298	line 3746 at a284420), exact-hypothesis wrapper: under the hypotheses of
   299	`uniform_series_tail_paper`, if also `E|u^{ε,δ}(1)|² ≤ B₁` for all `ε, δ > 0`,
   300	then `E|u|² ≤ B₁` for `u = Σ X_n`.  `IsProbabilityMeasure μ` is not used. -/
   301	theorem uniform_series_tail_second_moment_paper [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
   302	    (Y : ℝ → ℝ → ℕ → Lp ℝ 2 μ) (X : ℕ → Lp ℝ 2 μ) (r B B₁ : ℝ) (hr : 1 < r)
   303	    (hTW : ∀ ε δ : ℝ, 0 < ε → 0 < δ → TerminalWickInput μ (Y ε δ) r)
   304	    (hB : ∀ ε δ : ℝ, 0 < ε → 0 < δ →
   305	      ∫ ω, ((∑' n, r ^ n • Y ε δ n : Lp ℝ 2 μ) ω) ^ 2 ∂μ ≤ B)
   306	    (hX : ∀ n, Tendsto (fun p : ℝ × ℝ => Y p.1 p.2 n)
   307	      (𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ) ×ˢ 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ)) (𝓝 (X n)))

   309	      ∫ ω, ((∑' n, Y ε δ n : Lp ℝ 2 μ) ω) ^ 2 ∂μ ≤ B₁) :
   310	    ∫ ω, ((∑' n, X n : Lp ℝ 2 μ) ω) ^ 2 ∂μ ≤ B₁ := by
   311	  have hlim := (uniform_series_tail_paper Y X r B hr hTW hB hX).2.1
   312	  rw [integral_sq_eq_norm_sq]

   314	  filter_upwards [eventually_pos_pair] with p hp

   109	 3605|   times $\R^d$. Define $Y_0 = 1$ and

  3603	  \sup_{s,y}\E|\mathcal{W}(s,y)|^2 < \infty$, and that the field is jointly
  3604	  continuous in mean square on each open cell of a finite partition of $[0,T]$,
  3605	  times $\R^d$. Define $Y_0 = 1$ and

  3618	  (y_1,\ldots,y_m,z_1,\ldots,z_n)$. Then

  3621	    =\sum_{D\in\Pi_k}\mathcal{T}_{m,n,D}^{\mathcal{K}}(T,x),

  3627	      ={}&\int_{[0,T]^m_<\times[0,T]^n_<}
  3628	      \ud\boldsymbol s\,\ud\boldsymbol r
  3629	      \int_{(\R^d)^m\times(\R^d)^n}\\

  3641	  entrywise comparison $0 \le \mathcal{K}_1 \le \mathcal{K}_2$ compares all

  3649	  $\mathsf{g}_n^{T,x}$, integration at the last vertex gives $M_0 = 1$ and
  3650	  $M_n(T) = \int_0^T(T-s)M_{n-1}(s)\ud s$. Induction therefore yields $M_n(T) =
  3651	  T^{2n}/(2n)!$. Gaussian moments and H\"older's inequality give

    12	\begin{lemma}[The physical two-point integral]\label{L:spatial-physical-pair}
    13	  The positive measure $\nu(\ud x,\ud y) = \ud x\,\Gamma(\ud y)$ is
    14	  sigma-finite. For nonnegative functions define
    15	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-physical-pair}
    16	    B_\Gamma(f,h)=\int f(x)h(x-y)\nu(\ud x,\ud y)
    17	  \end{equation}

    19	  representatives of Lebesgue classes. Its value is representative independent.
    20	  Lebesgue-a.e. convergence transfers to $\nu$-a.e. convergence at both
    21	  positions $x$ and $x-y$.

    24	\begin{proof}

    26	  Lebesgue measure is sigma-finite. If $N$ is Borel and Lebesgue null, Tonelli
    27	  applied first in $x$ gives $\nu\{x\in N\} = 0$ and $\nu\{x-y\in N\} = 0$,
    28	  because every fixed translate of $N$ is null. An arbitrary Lebesgue null set
    29	  has a Borel null superset. Thus, arbitrary versions are measurable in the
    30	  $\nu$ completion with the same value, and the same observation applies to the
    31	  exceptional sets of a.e. convergence. Signed pairings will be used only after
    32	  absolute convergence. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-physical-pair}.

   230	  absolutely convergent and jointly continuous on $(H^1)^4$, with

   233	    \le R_0\prod_{j=1}^4N(f_j).

   236	  $R_0$. Every nonzero $H^1$ profile has $A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f) > 0$.

   239	\begin{proof}
   240	  For smooth compact $f$, normalization in $R_0$ proves
   241	  \eqref{E:spatial-homogeneous-bound}, including $f = 0$. All exponents in $N$
   242	  are positive and $N(f) \le \|f\|_{H^1}$. For smooth compact signed $Q,P$, the
   243	  absolute correlation is compactly supported and bounded by $\|Q\|_2\|P\|_2$.
   244	  Local finiteness of $\Gamma$ therefore makes its physical integral finite.
   245	  Smooth signed covariance is positive: with the ordinary transform
   246	  $\widehat{Q}_{\mathrm{ord}}(\xi) = \int e^{i\xi\cdot x}Q(x)\ud x$, the model
   247	  convention gives
   248	  \[
   249	    B_\Gamma(Q,Q)=\int|\widehat{Q}_{\mathrm{ord}}(\xi)|^2\mu(\ud\xi)
   250	    \ge0,\qquad Q\in C_c^\infty(\R^d;\R).
   251	  \]
   252	  Pair $\Gamma$ with the smooth compact correlation to obtain this identity;
   253	  rapid Fourier decay and tempered $\mu$ give finiteness. Evenness of $\Gamma$
   254	  and $(x,y)\mapsto(x-y,-y)$ give symmetry. The quadratic polynomial for $Q+tP$
   255	  gives covariance Cauchy--Schwarz. In particular, for smooth real $f,h$,
   256	  \[
   257	    0\le B_\Gamma(f^2,h^2)
   258	    \le R_0N(f)^2N(h)^2.
   259	  \]

   261	
   262	  Smooth compact functions are dense in $H^1$. Cutoffs equal to one on the
   263	  radius-$R$ ball, vanishing beyond $2R$ and with gradient at most $C/R$,
   264	  converge by the function and gradient tails and the bound $C\|f\|_2/R$ for the
   265	  extra gradient term. Mollification then converges in $H^1$ by $L^2$
   266	  translation continuity of the function and its weak gradients. The space is
   267	  separable through its closed isometric image $f\mapsto(f,\nabla f)$ in
   268	  $L^2(\R^d)^{d+1}$.
   269	
   270	  For arbitrary $f,h \in H^1$ take smooth approximants converging in $H^1$ and
   271	  along a common subsequence Lebesgue-a.e. Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-physical-pair}
   272	  transfers this convergence at both positions to $\nu$-a.e. convergence. Fatou
   273	  and continuity of $N$ give $B_\Gamma(f^2,h^2) \le R_0N(f)^2N(h)^2 < \infty$,
   274	  including the diagonal bound. At this stage Fatou supplies an inequality, not
   275	  continuity.
   276	
   277	  Apply ordinary Cauchy--Schwarz under the positive measure $\nu$ to
   278	  $f_1(x)f_3(x-y)$ and $f_2(x)f_4(x-y)$. The two squared integrals are finite by
   279	  the last bound; their square root is at most $R_0\prod_jN(f_j)$. This
   280	  proves~\eqref{E:spatial-four-linear}, absolute convergence and multilinearity.
   281	  Telescoping a difference one argument at a time and using $N(f) \le
   282	  \|f\|_{H^1}$ proves joint continuity. Thus, $A_{\mathrm{sp}}$ and the square
   283	  pairings are continuous. PSD for smooth compact profiles passes to finite
   284	  linear combinations of $H^1$ squares by this continuity, and its two-profile
   285	  Cauchy--Schwarz gives \eqref{E:spatial-square-CS}. This completes the physical
   286	  pairing argument beyond Fatou.
   287	
   288	  Every real unit $H^1$ profile has positive gradient energy by the Fourier
   289	  argument above. The homogeneous bound gives $R_{\mathrm{sp}} \le R_0$, and
   290	  smooth inclusion gives the reverse. Normalized smooth approximations preserve
   291	  the ratio by continuity. Finally, for nonzero $f$, choose a bounded set $E$ of
   292	  finite positive measure where $|f| \ge c > 0$. The correlation of $1_E$ is
   293	  continuous and positive near zero by $L^2$ translation continuity. An
   294	  origin-centered ball there has positive $\Gamma$ mass, so $A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f)
   295	  \ge c^4B_\Gamma(1_E,1_E) > 0$. This uses a nonnegative integral, not an $H^1$
   296	  claim for $1_E$. Finiteness was already proved. This proves
   297	  Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear}.
   298	\end{proof}

    22	\begin{lemma}[Inclusion into the covariance space and the smooth mean]
    23	  \label{L:positive-raw-embedding}

    25	  H_t\otimes G$ with
    26	  \begin{equation}\label{E:positive-bochner-inclusion}
    27	    \|J_GF\|^2
    28	    =\int_{I^2}K(s,t)\langle F(s),F(t)\rangle_G\ud s\ud t
    29	    \le K_0\|F\|_{L^2(I;G)}^2,\qquad K_0=\frac{2^a}{1-a}.
    30	  \end{equation}

    32	  $H_I$, with
    33	  \begin{equation}\label{E:positive-raw-mean}
    34	    \|\Psi\|_{H_I}^2=v_\Psi,\qquad
    35	    \mathcal{T}_R\Psi(s)=B_E(m_Rh_{\Psi,s})\quad\hbox{a.e. }s.
    36	  \end{equation}

    38	  every $R \ge 1$ and every $s \in I$.
    39	\end{lemma}

    43	  \[
    44	    \int_I K(s,t)\ud t
    45	    =\frac{s^{1-a}+(1-s)^{1-a}}{1-a}\le K_0 .
    46	  \]

    48	  give $\|Kf\|_2 \le K_0\|f\|_2$. The same estimate for absolute values bounds
    49	  the bilinear integral by $K_0\|f\|_2\|g\|_2$. Approximate scalar $L^2(I)$
    50	  functions by real $C_c^\infty(I)$ functions. This bound makes their original
    51	  test-null classes Cauchy in $H_t$, defines the bounded inclusion, and
    52	  identifies its pairing with the integral. Finite $G$-valued tensors then give
    53	  \eqref{E:positive-bochner-inclusion}. Simple fields are dense in Bochner
    54	  $L^2(I;G)$; the same bound on differences extends $J_G$. Absolute bilinear
    55	  continuity extends the integral identity as well.
    56	
    57	  For $G = H_{\mathrm{sp}}$, the Bochner integral $\int_IK(s,t)F(t)\ud t$ exists
    58	  almost everywhere: its norm is bounded by $K\|F\|(s)$, which belongs to $L^2$.
    59	  Simple-field approximation and the Schur estimate give a strongly measurable
    60	  $L^2$ version and a bounded map of norm at most $K_0$. On smooth finite
    61	  tensors it agrees with $(C_t\otimes I)J_G$ by the covariance definition.
    62	  Approximation by such tensors converges in $L^2(I;G)$. The integral converges

    64	  Lemma~\ref{L:uniform-mean-tensor} and~\eqref{E:positive-bochner-inclusion},

    69	  smooth $q$ supported there, the physical covariance gives
    70	  \begin{equation}\label{E:positive-local-spatial-bound}

    76	  white and singular Radon covariances. Thus, $t\mapsto\Psi_t$ is continuous,
    77	  bounded and compactly supported as an $H_{\mathrm{sp}}$-valued field, and
    78	  belongs to $L^2$. Its image under $J_{H_{\mathrm{sp}}}$ is the original test
    79	  class of $\Psi$. Indeed, the separated compact smooth approximants in
    80	  Lemma~\ref{L:cameron-supported-tensor} converge uniformly on one common
    81	  compact support. The local bound above and the temporal Schur estimate give
    82	  convergence both in $L^2(I;H_{\mathrm{sp}})$ and in the original covariance
    83	  norm. Their finite tensor identifications therefore have this same limit.
    84	  Formula~\eqref{E:positive-bochner-inclusion} and absolute Fubini give
    85	  \[
    86	    \|\Psi\|_{H_I}^2
    87	    =\int_{I^2}K(s,t)\langle\Psi_s,\Psi_t\rangle_{H_{\mathrm{sp}}}
    88	    \ud s\ud t
    89	    =\int_{I\times\R^d}\Psi(s,x)h_{\Psi,s}(x)\ud x\ud s=v_\Psi.

    94	  Test the spatial row~\eqref{E:uniform-mean-row} first with displacement $f$

   102	  Both resulting operators are bounded on $E$: the left by the mean theorem, the
   103	  right by the bounded smooth $h_{\Psi,s}$ and compact smooth mask. Dense states

   110	\end{proof}
